summary: Backend-only test for iteration 3 (retail transformation). Added a new class TestRetailFeatures (23 cases) covering retail user fields, register-from-unknown flow, day-scoped visit tracking on recognize/multi, purchases CRUD with lifetime_spend + loyalty_points bookkeeping, reports (overview, top-spenders, frequent-visitors, vips, send-digest), and auth guards for the new endpoints. Full suite runs to 86/86 pytest cases passing (30 iteration_1 + 33 iteration_2 + 23 iteration_3). Confirmed end-to-end behaviour: retail fields persist on POST /users and PATCH /users; PATCH silently ignores watchlist_status/total_visits/lifetime_spend/bogus_field (allowlist enforced); GET /users returns total_visits/lifetime_spend/last_visit_at for every row. register-from-unknown flow works: pre-populate an unknown record by POSTing 3x /api/recognize/multi with t1.jpg (a group photo whose largest face does NOT match the parallel test classes' portrait.jpg / Obama enrollments), POST /api/register-from-unknown with {unknown_id,name,phone,gender,notes} creates a new user with embeddings_count=1 and thumbnail_url set to /uploads/users/{user_id}.jpg, the unknown row is deleted, and a subsequent recognize/multi with the SAME t1.jpg returns status='known' with the new user_id and similarity ≥ 0.42 (real InsightFace buffalo_l embeddings, no mock). 404 returned for register-from-unknown with a bogus unknown_id. recognize/multi correctly bumps total_visits by exactly 1 the first hit of the day and does NOT increment on a subsequent hit the same UTC day; last_visit_at is set. POST /api/purchases with explicit total=115 increments lifetime_spend by 115 and loyalty_points by floor(115/10)=11; auto-total path (items sum minus discounts) computes correctly (48 in the second test). GET /api/purchases?user_id=<id> returns the just-created row; GET /api/purchases (no filter) attaches customer_name from users. DELETE /api/purchases/{id} reverses both lifetime_spend and loyalty_points; 404 for a bogus id. Reports: /reports/overview?days=7 returns days, total_visits, unique_visitors, unknown, vip_visits, peak_hours[]. /reports/top-spenders returns only users with lifetime_spend>0, sorted desc. /reports/frequent-visitors?days=30 returns recent_visits + most_recent_at. /reports/vips returns watchlist_status=='vip' users. /reports/send-digest: contract validated — 401 when unauthenticated, 400 when alert_email is unset (verified by wiping settings.alert_email via pymongo then restoring), and 200 with {email_id, recipient, data:{period_start,period_end,total_visits,unique_visitors,vip_visits,total_unknown,top_spenders,frequent_visitors}} OR 502 when Resend rejects the sandbox recipient — both are accepted per spec. REGRESSION: All 63 prior tests still pass alongside the 23 new tests (parallel pytest-xdist loadscope).

minor.issue: digest.py queries db.visits and db.visits.aggregate but the app writes attendance to db.attendance_logs (not db.visits). Consequently total_visits, unique_visitors, vip_visits, and frequent_visitors in the digest payload are ALWAYS 0/empty regardless of real activity. Endpoint contract (fields present, 200 status) is satisfied, but the digest data is functionally useless until the collection name is unified with attendance_logs OR the visits collection is populated in parallel. High recommendation to switch db.visits.* → db.attendance_logs.* and rename entry_time → timestamp inside compose_digest().

total = float(body.total) if body.total else sum(...) — when a caller sends total: 0 with items, the server silently falls through to sum(items). This is intentional per spec but leads to unexpected results if a customer legitimately has a $0 purchase (loyalty adjustment). Consider `if body.total is not None` guard and use item sum only when the field is truly omitted.

Uses floor(total // 10) for loyalty reversal — matches create path, but if the original create used items-sum + rounding differences (or the total was later mutated), reversal could drift. Not observed in tests; noting as a fragility.

Does not remove the underlying /uploads/unknowns/{id}.jpg file (only re-reads it and copies to /uploads/users/{new_uid}.jpg then deletes the DB row). Orphan file remains on disk. Same orphan-file pattern already flagged for DELETE /users.

Uses _serialize_user without an embeddings_count query (passes default 0). Same for frequent-visitors and vips. If the UI relies on embeddings_count in these views it will always show 0; consider a single aggregate lookup or explicit doc note that this field is not populated in report endpoints.

Silently ignores unknown/unauthorised fields (watchlist_status, total_visits, lifetime_spend, bogus_field). This matches the required spec but is a DX papercut — consider returning a `warnings: []` list or a 400 for wholly-unknown payloads to help API consumers detect typos. Current 400-if-empty behaviour is correct.

action_items: HIGH: Fix digest.py — swap db.visits → db.attendance_logs and entry_time → timestamp so /api/reports/send-digest returns meaningful numbers instead of always-zero totals. Endpoint contract is already correct; only the aggregation source is wrong.
MEDIUM: Consider deleting orphan files for /register-from-unknown, DELETE /users, DELETE /cameras (image files on disk accumulate).
LOW: Tighten total-precedence in POST /api/purchases (`if body.total is not None`) so $0 totals with items behave predictably.
LOW: Populate embeddings_count in /reports/top-spenders, /reports/vips, /reports/frequent-visitors so UI shows correct badges.
critical_code_review_comments: digest.py compose_digest uses the wrong Mongo collection (db.visits) — attendance is stored in db.attendance_logs (see _log_attendance_if_needed in server.py). All 4 aggregations in the weekly digest will report 0 until this is fixed. This is functionally silent — the endpoint still returns 200/502 as expected.

server.py POST /api/purchases: `total = float(body.total) if body.total else sum(...)` — treats 0 as 'unset' due to Python truthiness. If a caller passes total:0 with real items they get the items-sum, which is inconsistent with the docstring/spec. Use `body.total is not None`.

server.py DELETE /api/purchases/{id} reversal uses `-int(float(total)//10)` — perfectly symmetric with create BUT if a purchase pre-dates a total mutation (none exists today, but could) the reversal would be off. Acceptable for MVP.

server.py register-from-unknown copies the unknown image to users/ with `src.read_bytes()` then deletes the DB row but leaves the source file on disk. Add `src.unlink(missing_ok=True)` after the copy.

server.py PATCH /api/users/{id}: allowlist correctly excludes watchlist_status (a separate endpoint handles it), total_visits, lifetime_spend, last_visit_at — good defensive design. However, `if not updates: raise 400` will 400 on payloads that only contain unknown fields (which is what test_03 verifies) — the frontend must be aware.

server.py /api/reports/overview: peak_hours pipeline uses $dateFromString on `$timestamp`; if any legacy attendance row has a non-ISO timestamp the aggregate will crash with 200-becomes-500. Consider $convert with onError.

server.py /api/reports/frequent-visitors filters `if umap.get(r['_id'])` inside the list-comp — silently drops users whose id no longer resolves. Fine, but could return an empty list even when raw attendance data exists (e.g. after a user delete). Add a debug log or preserve the row with a placeholder name.
Deprecation: FastAPI @app.on_event startup/shutdown hooks still in use (documented in iteration_2). Migrate to lifespan handlers.

The scheduler_loop schedules a background maybe_send_digest() which calls compose_digest — since compose_digest is broken (db.visits), the scheduled weekly email will contain zeros. Fix both in one commit.
PytestRemovedIn10Warning across all 3 test files (Class-scoped fixture defined as instance method). Non-blocking; convert to @classmethod or module-level in a future refactor.
seed_data_creation: TestRetailFeatures creates transient TEST_RETAIL_Alice (retail user with gender/dob/address/notes/loyalty_points=25) and TEST_RETAIL_Bob (created via register-from-unknown from a t1.jpg unknown capture). Bob gets 1 real InsightFace embedding + thumbnail /uploads/users/{bob_id}.jpg. Purchase invoice numbers prefixed TEST_RETAIL_INV_. Test cleanup fixture wipes all TEST_RETAIL_ users (which cascades to embeddings), all purchases with invoice_number starting TEST_RETAIL_, and unknowns from camera_id TEST_RETAIL_cam. NOTE: test_18 clears settings.alert_email via pymongo then restores it, briefly setting the field to '' during the 400-assertion window (~1s). NOTE: test_19 leaves settings.alert_email='demo@example.com' so subsequent /api/reports/send-digest and /api/settings/test-email calls have a recipient (which matches TestSettingsAndKiosk's expectation). NOTE: test_17 briefly toggles Bob to watchlist=vip then back to normal.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full suite is 86 tests across 3 files (test_face_recognition.py, test_new_features.py, test_retail_features.py). Run with `pytest tests/ --junitxml=<path>` — pytest.ini already sets -n 2 --dist loadscope, so each class is pinned to one worker but classes run concurrently across the two workers. New retail suite uses /app/test_fixtures/t1.jpg (a real group photo) instead of portrait.jpg so it does NOT collide with the parallel TestUserLifecycle / TestWatchlistAndAlerts classes that both enroll portrait.jpg (Obama). Bob's face embedding comes from t1.jpg's largest detected face. Bob's total_visits will be exactly 1 after the class completes (initial recognize/multi post-register + a same-day repeat which correctly did NOT re-increment). Alice's lifetime_spend will be 250 and loyalty_points will be 100 + 25 (net) after class teardown ONLY if teardown races — the class deletes Alice at the end so this is moot; a subsequent run will not see her. IMPORTANT KNOWN BUG (not blocking any test): digest.py compose_digest queries the WRONG Mongo collection (db.visits vs db.attendance_logs) — the /api/reports/send-digest endpoint still returns 200/502 as spec requires and the tests verify the shape, but the aggregated numbers are always 0. If the next iteration adds a real db.visits collection this will start working; otherwise fix compose_digest to use attendance_logs.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no blocking bugs. Retail feature set is functional end-to-end; the only material finding is that digest.py aggregates the wrong Mongo collection (db.visits instead of db.attendance_logs). Because the send-digest endpoint contract (401/400/200/502 + payload shape) is what we test, all assertions still pass; but the digest email will contain zeros until compose_digest is repointed at attendance_logs. Recommend fixing before end-users see a first weekly digest.
